mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% month-over-month indicates weakening aggregate demand, which depresses earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST m/m change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below the median market return at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 97 for three consecutive months, absent a corresponding decline in unemployment (UNRATE < 6%), signals supply-side bottlenecks or demand weakness, which reduces earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 97 for three months AND UNRATE < 6%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant at 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% for two consecutive months signals an emergency easing, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts risk asset valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A strong acceleration in personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5% month-over-month) combined with rising housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household demand, which expands corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS m/m change > 0.5% AND HOUST m/m change > 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% for four consecutive months, with stable inflation (CPIAUCSL m/m change < 0.2%), signals a tight labor market with moderate inflation, which typically precedes higher wage growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% for four consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL m/m change < 0.2%
regime_hint: tight labor market with stable inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 102 for five consecutive months, accompanied by a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE m/m change within ±0.1%), indicates strengthening manufacturing and stable labor conditions, which supports earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when INDPRO > 102 for five months and UNRATE is stable (t-test p > 0.05).
